From 6c3118c32129b4197999a8928ba776bcabd0f5c4 Mon Sep 17 00:00:00 2001
From: "Chang S. Bae" <chang.seok.bae@intel.com>
Date: Fri, 10 Dec 2021 14:55:03 -0800
Subject: [PATCH] signal: Skip the altstack update when not needed

== Background ==

Support for large, "dynamic" fpstates was recently merged.  This
included code to ensure that sigaltstacks are sufficiently sized for
these large states.  A new lock was added to remove races between
enabling large features and setting up sigaltstacks.

== Problem ==

The new lock (sigaltstack_lock()) is acquired in the sigreturn path
before restoring the old sigaltstack.  Unfortunately, contention on the
new lock causes a measurable signal handling performance regression [1].
However, the common case is that no *changes* are made to the
sigaltstack state at sigreturn.

== Solution ==

do_sigaltstack() acquires sigaltstack_lock() and is used for both
sys_sigaltstack() and restoring the sigaltstack in sys_sigreturn().
Check for changes to the sigaltstack before taking the lock.  If no
changes were made, return before acquiring the lock.

This removes lock contention from the common-case sigreturn path.

[1] https://lore.kernel.org/lkml/20211207012128.GA16074@xsang-OptiPlex-9020/

Fixes: 3aac3ebea08f ("x86/signal: Implement sigaltstack size validation")
Reported-by: kernel test robot <oliver.sang@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Chang S. Bae <chang.seok.bae@intel.com>
Signed-off-by: Dave Hansen <dave.hansen@linux.intel.com>
Reviewed-by: Thomas Gleixner <tglx@linutronix.de>
Link: https://lkml.kernel.org/r/20211210225503.12734-1-chang.seok.bae@intel.com

diff --git a/kernel/signal.c b/kernel/signal.c
index a629b11bf3e0..dfcee3888b00 100644
--- a/kernel/signal.c
+++ b/kernel/signal.c
@@ -4185,6 +4185,15 @@ do_sigaltstack (const stack_t *ss, stack_t *oss, unsigned long sp,
 				ss_mode != 0))
 			return -EINVAL;
 
+		/*
+		 * Return before taking any locks if no actual
+		 * sigaltstack changes were requested.
+		 */
+		if (t->sas_ss_sp == (unsigned long)ss_sp &&
+		    t->sas_ss_size == ss_size &&
+		    t->sas_ss_flags == ss_flags)
+			return 0;
+
 		sigaltstack_lock();
 		if (ss_mode == SS_DISABLE) {
 			ss_size = 0;
-- 
2.25.1

### Modifications in Each File

**File: `kernel/signal.c`**
- Added a check in the `do_sigaltstack()` function to determine if there are any changes to the sigaltstack state before acquiring the `sigaltstack_lock()`.
- If no changes are detected (i.e., the current sigaltstack parameters match the requested ones), the function returns early with a value of `0`, avoiding the lock acquisition.

### Relationships
The modification improves performance by reducing lock contention in the common case of signal handling where no changes to the sigaltstack are necessary. By checking for changes before acquiring the lock, the patch addresses the performance regression caused by the new locking mechanism introduced in a previous commit. This change ensures that the signal handling path remains efficient when the sigaltstack state does not need to be updated.

The code statements that lead to the bug are:
```c
sigaltstack_lock();
if (ss) {
    ...
}
```
Reason:
The `sigaltstack_lock()` is acquired in the `sigreturn` path before checking if any changes are made to the sigaltstack state. This leads to unnecessary contention on the lock, causing performance regression during signal handling, especially in the common case where no changes are made.

The code statements that fix the bug are:
```c
if (t->sas_ss_sp == (unsigned long)ss_sp &&
    t->sas_ss_size == ss_size &&
    t->sas_ss_flags == ss_flags)
    return 0;
sigaltstack_lock();
```
Reason:
By checking if the sigaltstack parameters have changed before acquiring the lock, the code can return early without locking in cases where no changes are needed. This reduces lock contention and improves performance in the common case of unchanged sigaltstack parameters.
